q: my first bub I was super strict I didn’t have any of these as I was scared of the risks, I know the above aren’t recommended but I have done it with moderation but I’m still guilty and scared
cx: At 19 weeks with her second, looser with food and drink rules than the first time.

q: I really am not one to enjoy pregnancy and allowing myself these things with moderation is kindve giving me some kindve of ease lol
cx: Why she relaxed the rules this time.

q: Is there anything i should know? Look out for? Eat? Do? Besides the obvious vitamins, water, walking? Things to avoid? I have a pregnancy book but of course i finally get pregnant and i can’t find it.

q: Its too early to start telling people, i don’t have many friends and my sister and i aren’t the closest

cx: Near 20 weeks with her second, comparing gain with the first.

cx: Found out at about seven weeks in an emergency department.

q: Its been a struggle to get through work tonight because I’ve just been on the verge of tears since I got here.
cx: A night shift days after finding out.

q: one week i feel like he’s getting enough, im understanding him and the next i feel like he isn’t and i can’t read him and constantly wondering what he wants.
cx: Breastfeeding a five-week-old who was small at birth.

q: when he takes it as a top up i feel so defeated.
cx: Giving expressed milk in a bottle.

q: a couple times a week I wake up in the middle of the night and CANNOT fall back asleep. Recently this has been accompanied with this horrible internal crawling sensation all over my body.
cx: At 21 weeks, with a physical job.

q: It keeps me awake and I’m exhausted during the day. I work a pretty physical job and it suck’s so bad.
cx: Night waking meets a physical job.

q: My boyfriend feels he’s contributed a lot because whenever I ask him to do something, he’ll usually do it. The problem is that I feel like I’m carrying all of the mental load.
cx: Nine months pregnant, new relationship.

q: I have to think of everything, plan everything, ask for everything, and by the time I’ve asked, I could have just done it myself faster.
cx: Why asking him for help doesn't help.

q: He has mentioned being scared for me, but also brought up bringing a video game to the hospital for downtime which upset me.

q: He told me he’s spent far more on me than I’ve spent on baby items, and that he has other financial priorities.

q: maybe I do just need to delegate specific tasks, I’m almost 39 weeks so the end is near.
cx: Her own fix after the argument.

q: It never even occurred to me the sounds coming from your own body!! This made my skin crawl I won’t lie!!
cx: UK, planned birth in two days, reading others' experiences of theatre.

cx: A planned second pregnancy, nearly four-year-old at home.

q: I’d love to hear real experiences so I can set realistic expectations instead of assuming I’ll be back to normal in a few weeks.
cx: Planning to sit a four-hour certification exam after the birth.

q: I will be on maternity leave plus I can get help from MIL and FIL as they stay with us. My husband runs a business so im assuming he’ll be mostly out during the day but can help me at night.
cx: Her help plan for the newborn weeks.

q: Can you tell me what your experience was very early in pregnancy and if you have any advice of what to do at this point? Or what to expect?
cx: Hours after a planned positive test.

cx: Eight days after an easy second birth, worried she did too much.

q: I started Googling and i am panicked that i have a prolapse.
cx: A new feeling when peeing, a week after birth.

q: This isn't even my first pregnancy! When I was pregnant with my daughter I ate so well from the drop
cx: Nearly six weeks into her second pregnancy, nothing stays down.

q: I feel like I'm a tiny boat in the middle of the ocean, getting battered with wave after wave of nausea and I'm just clinging on to dear life.
cx: Describing her nausea at six weeks.

q: I'm chasing around a toddler ontop of this so it's a whole different level of difficult. My husband is home for the weekend and wonderful but when he's at work I have no village.
cx: Sickness while minding a toddler alone on weekdays.
